newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sembawang completes phase 1A of utilities complex.
newsitem.headline: Sembawang completes phase 1A of utilities complex.

text.p: Sembawang Utilities and Terminals Pte Ltd (SUT) said on Friday it had completed Phase 1A of a Singapore $250 million facility at Pulau Sakra, an island off Singapore.
The plant offers industrial support services ranging from the supply of steam, cooling water, demineralised and processed water, chemical storage and wastewater treatment, it said in a statement.
Phase 1A, valued at S$50 million, was designed and built to service the company's first chemical customer, Hoechst Acetyls Singapore Pte Ltd, SUT said.

SUT is led by Sembawang Engineering and Construction (SembEC), part of Singapore's Sembawang Corp. Other shareholders include Belgium's Tractebel Asia Pte Ltd, JTC International Pte Ltd (JTCI) and EDB Investment Pte Ltd (EDBI).

"Work on Phase 1B, representing a S$200-million expansion of Phase 1A's facilities, is already well underway, with completion and full commercial operations for SUT expected by early 1999," the statement said.
"Construction for Phase 1B had began in April in light of increasing utilities demands from SUT's growing number of clients."
SUT chairman Tan Tong Meng said that in Phase 2, the company planned to construct a 700-megawatt cogeneration plant, a type able to switch feedstock between fuel oil and natural gas.
Tan said plans for the plant were based on assumptions that piped natural gas from Indonesia would be available by 2000.

In April, SembEC signed an agreement with Indonesia's state-owned oil and gas company Pertamina for the supply of piped natural gas to Jurong Island. Pulau Sakra will later be merged with several small islands to become Jurong Island.
SembEC plans to import natural gas via a 480-km pipeline from Indonesia's West Natura fields, in the South China Sea, to be sold to power generators and chemical manufacturers on Jurong Island.
At present, SUT said it has obtained letters of intent from seven potential clients for the utility services.
The customers include Air Products Singapore, Eastman Chemical Company, Sumitomo Chemical Singapore, Asahi Chemical Industry, Poval Asia, Lonza Singapore and Van Ommeren Tank Terminal Singapore.
